title: Deck Staining in Gainesville, FL | Strip, Sand, Seal
description: Deck staining in Gainesville, FL: wash, strip, sand, board repair, and penetrating stain in transparent, semi-transparent, or solid. Free written estimate.
heroIntro: A gray, splintering deck is wood that has lost its protection. We clean it back to sound fibers, fix what is failing, and soak in a stain built for Florida sun and rain.

questions: How often should a deck be stained in Gainesville?
Should I use solid or semi-transparent deck stain in Florida?

sections.h2: Why Gainesville decks wear out so fast
body: A deck takes more punishment than any other painted or stained surface on a house. Horizontal boards hold rain and morning dew, sun cooks the top surface every afternoon, and pollen and leaf debris keep the wood damp underneath. In backyards across Gainesville, from the older lots near Duckpond to newer homes in Haile Plantation, the first sign is graying, followed by checking, splinters, and mildew in the shaded corners.
Once the wood fibers on the surface break down, fresh stain has nothing sound to soak into. That is why we never just roll new stain over old.

bullets: Moisture readings to confirm the wood is dry enough to take stain
Strip and sand failing stain back to a clean substrate
Board replacement and hardware fixes for loose, cracked, or soft boards
Penetrating stain, sprayed and back-brushed into the grain
Railings, stairs, and skirting included when listed on the estimate

body: Transparent stain shows the most grain but needs the most frequent recoating in full Florida sun. Semi-transparent is a middle ground that tones the wood while letting grain read through. Solid stain behaves more like paint and hides mismatched replacement boards, but on walking surfaces it can wear in traffic lanes.

Many Gainesville owners choose semi-transparent on the deck floor and solid on railings and skirting. We will show you samples on your own boards before deciding. If the deck was painted in the past, the conversation changes: paint on a walking surface traps moisture and peels, so the estimate will say whether we strip it back to bare wood or continue with a solid coating. Our deck and fence staining service page explains each product in more depth.

Stain needs dry wood and a dry forecast. Fall through spring is ideal; in summer we schedule early in the day and watch radar. After stripping and washing, the deck has to dry before stain goes on, which is why deck projects usually span a few days even when the staining itself goes quickly.

Wondering whether yours is past saving? Our guide to signs of deck wood rot shows what to check. Fences usually weather the same way, so many clients add fence staining in Gainesville to the same visit, along with a pressure wash for walkways and drives. The rest of our local work is listed on the Gainesville painting contractor page.

faqs.q: How often does a Gainesville deck need re-staining?
faqs.a: It depends on sun exposure, opacity, and foot traffic. Transparent finishes need attention sooner than solid ones, and fully sunny decks wear faster than shaded ones.

faqs.q: Can you stain a brand-new pressure-treated deck right away?
faqs.a: New treated lumber usually needs time to dry before it will absorb stain. A moisture reading tells us when it is ready.
Yes. Board replacement and hardware fixes are part of the prep and are itemized on the estimate.
